mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above the prior 12-month average predicts a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to tightened discounting of future cash flows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the 12-month prior average (t-test p > 0.05) during the trigger period.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly PAYEMS rises above its 6-month moving average, labor market strength is interpreted as supporting corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 6-month prior average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in HOUST (industrial production) below its 4-month moving average indicates weakening demand, which is associated with negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < HOUST_4M_avg for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in at least 70% of such contraction episodes (empirical frequency).

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO falls below its 3-month moving average, it signals supply-side constraints that reduce expected corporate profit margins, resulting in a negative S&P 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: No significant negative return in 20-day horizon during confirmed supply shocks (as identified by three consecutive INDPRO drops).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained dual increase in both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE above their 12-month averages creates a risk-off environment, producing negative S&P 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > FEDFUNDS_12M_avg AND UNRATE > UNRATE_12M_avg for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05) during the trigger period.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 5%, it reflects labor market slack and is associated with a positive S&P 60-day forward return as investors anticipate lower wage growth and potential rate cuts.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the 12-month pre-trigger average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in GDPC1 (real GDP) above the 2-quarter moving average, accompanied by a decline in CPIAUCSL, suggests a strong demand recovery and positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05) during the episode.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) falls for three consecutive months below its 12-month average, it indicates weak consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < RSAFS_12M_avg for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During such episodes, 20-day forward returns are not significantly worse than the 12-month pre-weakness average (t-test p > 0.05).
